# Share bounded predicate waits across dock consumers

## Context

The [bounded loop audit](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5562606384) found eight matching Boolean wait bodies across Workstation and DemoB. The other seven matching loop headers contain gesture actuation, receipt returns or readiness snapshots and are excluded. This is one small implementation cut under the existing workspace-decomposition epic.

## The Problem

Each consumer repeats attempt bounds, delay scheduling, early success and final predicate sampling. Those mechanics depend only on the instance lifecycle, while the predicates depend on the consumer. Copying the mechanics makes their destruction and retry behavior independently editable.

## The Architectural Reality

`src/core/Base.mjs` already owns `timeout()` and `trap()`. Its timeout registers a rejection which `destroy()` settles with `Neo.isDestroyed`. Both consumer classes inherit Base through their ordinary families; no dock-specific collaborator or configuration bridge is needed.

A live import probe reports `Base.prototype.waitFor === undefined`, with `timeout` and `trap` both functions. Source searches across `src`, `apps` and `examples` found no conflicting `waitFor` method.

## The Fix

Add `Base#waitFor(predicate, {attempts=120, delay=16}={})` for a synchronous Boolean predicate. Reuse `this.timeout(delay)`; retain the existing loop's immediate sample, bounded waits, early success, and final predicate read. Propagate predicate exceptions and timeout rejection.

Replace only the eight simple Boolean wait bodies in `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` and `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs`. Keep their predicates, caller defaults and public methods. Extend the existing core timeout unit spec and regenerate the tracked size baseline.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| New Base.waitFor | Existing Base timeout/trap lifecycle | Synchronous predicate sampled immediately; at most attempts waits; true exits early; one final sample after exhaustion | Boolean false on exhaustion; exceptions and destruction rejection propagate | Method JSDoc | Immediate/delayed success, exhaustion/final sample, throwing predicate, actual destroy |
| Eight consumer waits | Existing consumer predicates and signatures | Delegate repeated polling mechanics through inherited Base method | Preserve current attempts/delay and return values | Existing consumer intent retained | Focused consumer suites and full unit suite |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Base owns one documented predicate-wait implementation using its existing timeout lifecycle, with no dock-specific state.
- [ ] Eight matching Boolean loop copies are removed; their predicates and caller defaults remain in the two consumers.
- [ ] Controls verify immediate success, bounded delays, final sampling, predicate failure and `Neo.isDestroyed` rejection during a pending wait.
- [ ] Existing consumer behavior remains green; focused and full unit suites pass, and the size baseline records the consumer reduction.

## Out of Scope

The seven gesture/snapshot/receipt loops; async predicates; event subscription machinery; native park/admission/recovery changes; other factory conversions; modifying existing approved PRs; Brain/tooling work.

## Avoided Traps

A new helper class or controller with consumer callbacks/configs; putting consumer predicates into Base; treating all matching loop headers as equivalent; converting destruction rejection into false; changing retry semantics while extracting them.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029; no docking or native authority changes.
Decision Record: no new ADR required for this additive lifecycle utility.
